newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MAJOR FOREIGN INTEREST SEEN IN S.AFRICAN MEDIA.
newsitem.headline: MAJOR FOREIGN INTEREST SEEN IN S.AFRICAN MEDIA.

text.p: Foreign entertainment, media and communications (EMC) companies looking to expand their markets are actively looking for partners in South Africa, business services company Price Waterhouse said on Thursday.

"Expansion is the name of the game," Wilhelm Krige, head of the company's EMC division in South Africa, told a seminar at the Southern African International Film and Television Market being held in Cape Town.

"Sixty percent of my time currently is being taken up by entertaining overseas EMC companies that are actively out here looking for partners in South Africa... South Africa has become a focus for the international community," Krige said.
He said good weather and relatively cheap costs were also attracting foreign film and television makers.
"I expect to see a lot of companies moving in and utilising South Africa as a place to film movies. Most will want to find partners here."
Krige said local firms would do well to align with the foreign players who had technological and financial resources lacking in South Africa.
He said rapidly changing communications technology like digital satellite television was changing the playing field for advertisers and film makers.
"New technology brings new distribution channels... It makes it increasingly difficult to focus -- bigger choice, more confusion.
"Advertisers will have a major problem because it's going to be very difficult to determine where your advertising-spend should go at the end of the day," Krige said.

He said this also meant the people providing television content would have to become brand conscious, because television watchers would try to resolve their confusion over which channel to choose by going for "brands" of entetainment or news.
"It will be increasingly difficult for consumers to decide what they're going to watch, and then branded content will be very important.
"If you have a choice of 10 movies to watch, chances are eight out of 10 that you'll switch to the Disney channel, because of the name Disney.
"If you want news, and there's 100 news channels available, your chance of switching to CNN is going to be nine out of 10," Krige said.
